instance_name.description: The name or relative resource id of the instance that owns the table.
instance_name.rationale: Identifies which Bigtable instance contains the table for IAM. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

table.description: The name or relative resource id of the table to manage IAM policies for.
table.rationale: Table scoped by this IAM binding or member. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

member/members.description: Identities granted the privilege in `role` (for `google_bigtable_table_iam_member` or `google_bigtable_table_iam_binding`). Each entry can be one of: **allUsers**, **allAuthenticatedUsers**, **user:{email}**, **serviceAccount:{email}**, **group:{email}**, **domain:{domain}**.
member/members.rationale: Public principals on table IAM expose table data access to broad unaudited audiences.

role.description: The role that should be applied. Only one `google_bigtable_table_iam_binding` can be used per role. Custom roles must use `[projects|organizations]/{parent-name}/roles/{role-name}`. See [Bigtable roles](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/access-control#roles).
role.rationale: IAM role granted at table scope. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

policy_data.description: For `google_bigtable_table_iam_policy` only: the policy data generated by a `google_iam_policy` data source.
policy_data.rationale: Full IAM policy document for policy-style resources. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

project.description: The project in which the table belongs. If it is not provided, Terraform will use the provider default.
project.rationale: GCP project for the table IAM resource. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.
